summary: YES on the core promise. (2) A spec BOTH build loops reach is withheld whatever order they run in - seen.add is after every gate, so the single application point in _add holds. (3) Duplicate spec ids: I reproduced the last-wins harm (a draft prerequisite reading as shipped from a second file, releasing dependent work) and check_spec_ids refuses it (1 error); the residual that readers stay last-wins is declared in the spec. (4) A dependency naming a spec that does not exist resolves to DEP_ABSENT, is named in the withheld report, and unrelated work is still offered. (5) Six depends_on shapes: every shape that crashes the reader (list-of-mappings, nested list) is refused by check_depends_on, as are a bare scalar, None, a mapping and an integer member; the one shape the contract admits reads without raising. (6) NON-STARVATION: a three-member dependency cycle plus a self-cycle plus an unrelated ready spec returned in 0.001s with no hang and no exception - each cycle member withheld individually, the unrelated unit still offered. (7) Review units with an unshipped dependency and with an absent dependency are both still offered as review work and appear in no withheld report, on the standalone and the planned lane. On the live corpus: 154 specs, 13 at ready, 7 claimable, 5 dependency-withheld (exactly the five AC2 names, at the states it names), and zero claimable build units with an unmet dependency.
